rules.description: An exhibition is reframed as a public visibility milestone.
rules.rationale: Both events can signal recognition within a relevant network.
rules.limitation: An exhibition does not demonstrate market demand or commercial traction.
rules.missingMessage: No exhibition records included in this dataset.

rules.description: Gallery representation is reframed as an institutional backer relationship.
rules.rationale: Both describe an established organization committing its reputation and infrastructure to a practice.
rules.limitation: A gallery's commission and obligations differ from an investor's, and representation terms are rarely public.
rules.missingMessage: Gallery representation not recorded in selected sources.

rules.description: A museum acquisition is reframed as an anchor-customer style adoption.
rules.rationale: Both record a large, durable institution choosing to take on what a practice produces.
rules.limitation: An acquisition is a cultural-memory decision, not recurring revenue, and the price is often not disclosed.
rules.missingMessage: No acquisition records included in this dataset.

rules.description: A residency is reframed as an incubation or acceleration period.
rules.rationale: Both give time, space and a network to a project before it is expected to stand alone.
rules.limitation: Residencies rarely ask for equity or a growth outcome.
rules.missingMessage: No residency records included in this dataset.

rules.description: An artist statement describing a long-term inquiry is reframed as a market thesis.
rules.rationale: Both state a durable problem space that the work keeps returning to.
rules.limitation: An inquiry is not a market; it may be deliberately unsellable. The Office quotes the statement and does not summarize it.
rules.template: Problem space, as stated in source: “{text}”
rules.missingMessage: No artist statement in selected sources. Collection records rarely include one.

rules.description: A funding round is reframed through the language of patronage.
rules.rationale: Both involve external financial support for a proposed future.
rules.limitation: Venture investment is not equivalent to artistic patronage.
rules.missingMessage: Funding history not available in selected sources.

rules.description: Joining an accelerator is reframed as admission to a recognized network, like a residency or a curated group show.
rules.rationale: Both are selection events in which an institution's name attaches to an emerging practice.
rules.limitation: Accelerator selection criteria and obligations differ from curatorial ones, and listing in a directory is weaker evidence than being selected in a named year.
rules.missingMessage: Accelerator affiliation not recorded in selected sources.

rules.description: A product launch is reframed as the premiere of a work.
rules.rationale: Both mark the first time something is shown to a public.
rules.limitation: A product is expected to be iterated and scaled; a premiere is usually a fixed event.
rules.missingMessage: No product launch records included in this dataset.

rules.description: A company's public description of what it does or will do is reframed as a curatorial proposition.
rules.rationale: Both are short public statements that ask an audience to imagine a future.
rules.limitation: Marketing language is not a curatorial argument. The Office quotes the source text and does not infer funding, revenue or traction from it.
rules.template: Curatorial proposition, as stated in source: “{text}”
